title: Attention kernel sequencer with confidence-based fallback playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Reduce latency/regression incidents caused by aggressive FlashAttention v3 activations by sequencing kernel choices using a runtime confidence signal. We will build a lightweight kernel sequencer that consults per-request and per-tenant confidence heuristics to decide: prefer v3, prefer v2, or route to a safer generic kernel. The sequencer must be cheap (<=1-2% added CPU per request), respect SLOs (p95 decode latency target unchanged), and allow staged rollouts with automatic rollback based on quality and latency telemetry.

Design summary: compute a confidence score composed of 1) request shape heuristics (tokens, batch size, head count), 2) recent kernel success rate and latency deltas (sliding window), 3) KV-cache warmness and prefix-match ratio. Score -> action mapping is configurable via runtime policy: {high -> v3, medium -> v3 with guarded warmup, low -> v2, critical -> safe-generic}. Implement a short-term adaptation loop that decays historical confidence and weights recent failures more heavily to catch regressions quickly. Provide per-tenant overrides and an opt-out tag for enterprise Dedicated clusters.

Telemetry & metrics: add kernel_choice, confidence_score, reason_code to request traces. Primary signals for rollout: p95 decode latency, kernel error rate, token-generation quality regressions (measured by eval prompt set mismatch and surprise scoring), and increased memory OOMs. Alert thresholds and automated rollback rules are defined in the playbook.

Experimentation plan: run offline replay on our replay-bench with representative tenant mixes; run canary on 2% traffic skewed toward synthetic stress workloads, then 10%, 25% and global. Each phase runs for a minimum of 72h with postmortem checks. Performance gates: p95 latency within +5% of baseline, kernel error rate < 0.1% above baseline, no statistically significant degradation on core eval sets.

Rollout & failure mode handling: automatic immediate rollback on any gate breach. On rollback we capture failing request traces and surgical repro runs. Provide a quarantine mechanism for tenants that repeatedly trigger low-confidence routing so they are pinned to conservative kernels while we debug.

Acceptance criteria: (1) 95th percentile decode latency across canary is within targets, (2) observability surfaces show confidence signal is well-calibrated (correlation >0.7 with actual kernel success), (3) automated rollback works end-to-end, (4) documentation and SDK flags available for customers.
comments: 2025-01-12 Maya Chen: Initial triage and design sketched in team meeting. Decided to use a composite confidence signal rather than a single threshold to reduce oscillation.

2025-01-22 Liam O'Connor: Prototype sequencer implemented in runtime branch feat/kernel-sequencer. Local microbench on A100 shows 0.9% CPU overhead and variable p95 improvement on long-context traces. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4832

2025-01-30 Maya Chen: Replay bench results: 2% of tenants with irregular head_counts see p95 regressions on bare v3; sequencer with conservative policy eliminated regressions and preserved v3 benefits for 68% of traffic. Proceeding to 2% canary next cycle. Added detailed telemetry fields to trace schema.
2025-02-03 SRE oncall: Canary at 2% started; first 24h stable. Observability dashboards prepared under Console -> KernelSequencer. Next checkpoint scheduled 2025-02-06.
